Mateo / team —

Summary proposal (concise tiers we can offer to customers):

1) Fast Erase (32-hour SLA) — tenant-scoped full deletion
- What: Remove all indexed records and cached KV prefixes for the tenant across hosted runtime. Purge mirrors/replicas in primary region.
- Constraints: Does not immediately remove on-disk backups (we can mark for deletion and rotate next backup window). Recommend contractual retention floor of 30 days for backup overwrite unless customer purchases escrow/fast-backup-rotation add-on.
- Audit artifacts: deletion job id, per-shard deletion checksums, time-stamped manifest, and a signed statement of completion (PDF).

2) Field Redact + Retain (24-hour enactment) — pseudonymize selected fields but keep record skeletons for analytics
- What: Server-side deterministic tokenization or irreversible hash of configurable fields (name, SSN, MRN). We can also zero out free-text spans flagged as PHI via our content redaction pipeline.
- Constraints: Redaction is irreversible for hashed fields. For text spans we use a safe-mask approach: replace tokens with [REDACTED:FIELDTYPE] while keeping surrounding text. This preserves downstream model context at lower fidelity.
- Audit artifacts: redaction matrix (fields redacted, hash salts used), redaction job log, sample pre/post diffs for a small sampling (with customer approval).

3) Selective Cache Evict + Archive (72-hour initial, longer for cold archives) — hybrid for long-term compliance
- What: Evict active KV caches and runtime caches quickly; move deeper storage to encrypted cold archive with retention policy gated by region.
- Constraints: Archive deletion windows depend on underlying storage provider’s deletion schedule; typical cold-delete can be 90 days.
- Audit artifacts: archive manifest, storage provider deletion receipts when available.

Implementation notes:
- For PHI we recommend defaulting to Option 2 (Field Redact) if customers want to retain analytics but remove identifiers. If they require cryptographic erasure, Option 1 is the path but requires backup rotation terms.
- If routing across regions, erasure must run in every region containing replicas — time to global completion varies by region.
- For on-prem/private deployments we can support more aggressive backup rotation under contract.

I’ve attached a redaction_matrix_v1.xlsx to map which fields and redaction modes we support.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Privacy Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com

Date: Sat, 04 Oct 2025 10:22:33 -0700
Subject: Re: PHI retention windows + redaction options — quick Q

Adding operational & security considerations: 

- Evidence chain: We can produce an export of the deletion job with SHA256 hashes of affected object ids, signed with our HSM-backed key, plus a time-stamped manifest. That should satisfy InfoSec for proof-of-action.
- Logs: We retain system-level audit logs (non-PII) for 180 days by default; however, per-tenant log slices that contain redacted content can be configured to shorter windows. If a customer requires total removal of logs containing PHI, we can schedule a targeted wipe, but need to document the scope in the MA.
- Backups & escrow: For full cryptographic deletion we recommend an escrow/backup rotation clause that allows us to purge backup copies in X days (typical windows: 30 / 90 / 180 days). Without that clause, we can mark backups and guarantee deletion on next backup cycle.
- For private deployments: we can run immediate zeroize scripts that overwrite disk sectors and provide a certificate of zeroize. That is only available under private or dedicated capacity contracts.

Security note: please ensure customers understand redacting free text does not guarantee removal of inferred identifiers embedded across context; recommend field tokenization for high-risk identifiers.

-Marcus
Head of Infrastructure Security, Redwood Inference

From: rachel_kim@redwood.com

Couple of legal points for the proposed tiers — for inclusion in the brief to MedAssist: 

- SLA language: for Fast Erase (32-hour SLA) we should add an exception for restored backups from third-party cloud snapshots where deletion may be delayed until snapshot lifecycle completes — propose adding: "Deletion SLA applies to primary runtime and replicated storage; backup purging occurs per backup rotation schedule unless escrow add-on purchased."
- Evidence: we can provide signed manifests and deletion job IDs but should avoid claiming erasure of 3rd-party-managed backups unless we have contractual control.
- Contract terms: add options for a backup-rotation addendum (30/90/180) and a Private Zeroize addendum. Draft a short clause and attach to the response.

I’ll draft suggested clause text and the customer-facing summary for Monday.

-Rachel
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Hi Claire —

Thanks for the clear ask. Based on internal review we propose the following customer-ready summary and next steps (attached):

1) Options we can offer you (summary):
- Fast Erase (recommended if you require cryptographic removal of tenant data from active systems) — 32-hour primary runtime SLA; backup purge subject to backup rotation addendum (30/90/180).
- Field Redact (recommended for analytics + compliance balance) — 24-hour enactment for configured fields; irreversible hashing/tokenization for identifiers; free-text safe-mask for narrative PHI.
- Selective Cache Evict + Archive — hybrid flow for long-term retention with archive deletion receipts when available.

2) Evidence you will receive: signed deletion manifests (HSM key), per-shard checksums, time-stamped job id, and redaction matrix showing which fields were tokenized.

3) Legal & procurement asks: we’ll include an optional backup-rotation addendum and a Private Zeroize addendum if you need faster backup purges. Rachel will follow up with clause text.

Next steps: I attached a redaction matrix and a short SOC2 excerpt showing the export pathway. If you’d like, we can schedule a 30-minute call Tuesday to walk the InfoSec team through the artifacts and addendum choices.

Best —
Mateo
Product Manager, Privacy Integrations
Redwood Inference
